result.title: Sampling and Curvature in First-Exit Comparisons for Momentum SGD
result.summary: First-exit prediction for momentum SGD depends on sampling information that pointwise gradient laws omit. Strongly convex finite pools with identical pointwise laws and matched iid momentum dynamics can have different reshuffled exits; even analytic pools with uniformly close pointwise laws can have separated exit probabilities. For persistent sampling in one dimension, we establish an explicit $O(h)$ mean-exit comparison with a finite-rate switching process under nonvanishing component velocities and step-size conditions; iid sampling instead averages to an ODE. Retaining realized minibatches and sampled curvature yields finite-window exit brackets beyond this regime. In 32 trained ridge-logistic runs, 29 meet prespecified targets with rounding-certified brackets; an enclosure control explains most of the width advantage. Exact-real certificates establish finite means at the original tested radii for three ResNet-18 checkpoints and give local finite-mean conditions for tanh and ViT networks; their upper bounds remain loose, and original-radius ViT mean guarantees remain unresolved despite 128 fresh continuation paths. A two-network replication gives 32/32 successful seeds in each of four finite-path persistence comparisons. Independent equal-length controls retain slower exits after refresh resets than without resets, but the refresh-versus-random ordering reverses with update length at both networks. These interventions do not causally decompose raw momentum SGD. Neural step-size scaling does not validate the switching limit.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 momentum SGD 的首次退出（first-exit）预测为何依赖逐点梯度律所忽略的采样信息，比较持续采样与 iid 采样下的平均退出行为，并用有限窗口退出括号、实数证书及训练实验加以检验。
AI.relevance_reason: 首次退出时间可视为一类停止时刻分析，其对采样方式与曲率的敏感性，可能与 LVR 中「何时停止」的停止决策如何随证据采样而变化的问题存在概念联系，属可供核查的远域线索，但材料未涉及任何多模态或 latent 推理内容。
